# AGENTS.md

## Project Context

PromptFlow — a node-based visual canvas for chaining LLM prompts (React Flow + OpenRouter). Full spec, tech stack, and phase breakdown live in `@.agents/plan/PLAN.md` — read it before starting any task, not just when confused.

**Stack:** TypeScript (strict), React + Vite, `@xyflow/react`, Zustand, Tailwind, OpenRouter via OpenAI-compatible SDK. Don't introduce a different framework, state library, or styling approach without asking first.

## Commands

<!-- Fill these in once the project is scaffolded — agents rely on this to verify their own work -->
- Install: `npm install`
- Dev server: `npm run dev`
- Build: `npm run build`
- Lint: `npm run lint`
- Test: `npm run test`
- Typecheck: `npm run typecheck`

## Response Style

- Keep responses concise by default. Only go long if I explicitly ask for detail or a walkthrough.
- No filler summaries of what you're about to do — just do it, then report what changed.

## Planning Mode

- Never assume design, tech stack, or feature scope — ask before proceeding.
- Ask clarifying questions **up front, batched together**, not one at a time mid-task.
- Check `@.agents/plan/PLAN.md` first for anything already decided — don't re-ask questions it already answers.
- If a request conflicts with something in `PLAN.md`, flag the conflict explicitly instead of silently picking one.

## Change / Edit Mode

- Work phase by phase, exactly as broken down in `PLAN.md`. Stop after each phase and wait for my feedback before starting the next — don't chain phases together automatically.
- Prefer delegating implementation work to subagents over doing it yourself directly, when a subagent setup exists for the task type.
- Show a short summary of what changed after each phase (files touched, key decisions made) — not the full diff unless asked.

## Model Tiers

- **Planning, review, and multi-step implementation:** use the strongest available free-tier model.
- **Routine/system tasks** (installs, boilerplate scaffolding, running commands, formatting): use the lightest/cheapest available model — no need to burn a strong model on mechanical work.
- If unsure which tier a task falls into, default to the stronger model rather than risk broken code from a weaker one.

## Subagents

- use the global agent ui-interactivity-tester when checking the UI
- Define subagents under `.opencode/agent/` (project-level) with `mode: subagent` and an explicit `model:` field per the tier rules above.
- Use them for scoped, well-defined tasks (e.g. a review-only agent, a test-writing agent) rather than open-ended "build the feature" delegation — keep me in the loop on anything architectural.

## Codebase Navigation (graphify)

A knowledge graph of this repo lives in `graphify-out/` (`graph.json`, `GRAPH_REPORT.md`). Use it before raw text search.

- **Query first.** For any question about structure, relationships or "where/what calls/what depends on" — run `graphify query "<question>"` (or `graphify path "A" "B"` / `graphify explain "<symbol>"`) **before** using `grep`, `find` or reading files to explore. Skim `graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md` for the god nodes and community map when starting on an unfamiliar area.
- **Then verify in source.** Treat graph answers as a map: read the cited `source_file`/`source_location` before editing, and trust the code over the graph if they disagree. `INFERRED`/`AMBIGUOUS` edges are hints, not facts.
- **Fall back to grep/Read** only for exact-string lookups (a literal, a CSS class, a log message), for files the graph doesn't cover, or when the graph is missing or visibly stale.
- **Update after changes.** After code edits (and before committing), refresh the graph with `graphify update .` (AST only, no LLM, no API key). After changing docs (`AGENTS.md`, `README.md`) or images, run `/graphify . --update` instead so semantic nodes are re-extracted. Commit the refreshed `graphify-out/graph.json`, `GRAPH_REPORT.md` and `manifest.json` with the change, as their own `chore(graph)` commit.
- Never hand-edit files in `graphify-out/`; rebuild them.

## Code Conventions

<!-- Fill in as they stabilize -->
- TypeScript strict mode, no `any` without a comment explaining why.
- Functional components + hooks only, no class components.
- One component per file, colocate related types in the same file unless shared across modules (then → `src/types/`).

### Chain LLM prompts on a canvas. Run them. See every step. A visual, node-based playground for building multi-step prompt flows. Wire up inputs, prompts and models, branch and merge, then watch the results stream in, with the cost of every run in plain sight. The built-in Compare two takes example, after a run.
--- ## Why you might like it - **See the whole chain.** Every step is a node you can read, edit and rerun. No hidden prompts. - **Bring any key.** Paste a key and PromptFlow works out the provider and lists the models _that key_ can use. - **No backend.** Requests go straight from your browser to the provider. Your key never touches a server of ours, because there isn't one. - **Know what it cost.** Tokens, cost and time for every run and every step, before and after. - **Built to be driven fast.** Command palette, undo/redo, auto-layout, and a keyboard shortcut for nearly everything. ## Features | | | | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Five node types** | **Input** → **Prompt** (templates with `{{input}}`) → **Agent** (any model) → **Merge** (join branches) → **Output** (rendered Markdown). | | **Six providers** | OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Groq and Mistral. One key at a time; the provider is detected from the key. | | **Branch and merge** | One node can feed many. A Merge node joins them back in canvas order, optionally with each branch's name above its text. | | **Variables** | Write `{{topic}}` anywhere and fill it in from the Variables dialog. Reuse one flow for different content. | | **Live results** | Text streams into the Output node as it is generated. Failed steps show why and have a **Retry** that reruns only from there. | | **Reports** | Download a run (or any run from history) as one clean Markdown report: result first, then every step with its model, tokens and cost. | | **Saved flows** | Name a flow and it autosaves in your browser. Switch between flows, duplicate, rename, export and import as JSON (your key is never exported). | | **Make it yours** | Every node resizes. Text size is adjustable globally and per node. Light and dark themes, or follow your system. | | **Edit with confidence** | Undo/redo, copy/paste/duplicate, Tidy auto-layout, minimap, and an Undo toast whenever something replaces your canvas. | | **Accessible** | Keyboard-operable dialogs and menus, status that never relies on colour alone, reduced-motion support, and axe-clean in both themes. | ## Quick start ```bash npm install npm run dev ``` Open the app, then: 1. **Add your API key** in Settings (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Groq or Mistral). 2. **Pick an example** on the empty canvas, or build your own from **Add node**. 3. **Press Run** on the Output node (or Ctrl/⌘ + Enter). > Node 22 is what CI uses. ### Keyboard shortcuts | Shortcut | Does | | ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | | Ctrl/⌘ + K | Command palette: any action, or jump to a node by name | | Ctrl/⌘ + Enter | Run the flow | | Esc | Stop a running flow | | Ctrl/⌘ + Z / Shift + Z | Undo / redo | | Ctrl/⌘ + C / V / D | Copy / paste / duplicate selected nodes | | F / Shift + F | Zoom to selection / fit everything | | ? | How PromptFlow works | ## How a flow works ``` Input ──► Prompt ──► Agent ─┐ ├──► Merge ──► Prompt ──► Agent ──► Output Input ──► Prompt ──► Agent ─┘ ``` - A **Prompt** inserts the text arriving from the previous node with `{{input}}`, and a variable with `{{name}}`. - An **Agent** sends the prompt to the model you chose, with an optional system prompt, temperature, token limit, JSON output and fallback models. - Independent branches run side by side, then wait for each other at a **Merge**. - Selecting a node opens its settings; dragging a corner resizes it. ## Privacy - Flows, settings and run history live in your browser's `localStorage`. Nothing is uploaded. - Your API key is stored separately (this tab only by default) and sent only to its own provider. - A dev-only fallback key can go in `.env.local` (see `.env.example`). It is ignored in production builds, because Vite inlines `VITE_*` values into the bundle. ## Tech TypeScript (strict) · React 18 · Vite · [`@xyflow/react`](https://reactflow.dev) · Zustand · Tailwind CSS · Zod · Vitest · Playwright ``` src/ ├─ components/ canvas, nodes, panels, dialogs, palette, toolbar ├─ engine/ flow execution, scheduling, retries, cost estimates ├─ lib/ providers, serialization, layout, reports, variables ├─ store/ graph, run, settings, model catalog, history, saved flows └─ types/ shared types e2e/ Playwright end-to-end tests ``` ## Scripts | Command | What it does | | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | | `npm run dev` | Start the Vite dev server | | `npm run build` | Typecheck and build | | `npm run typecheck` | `tsc -b --noEmit` | | `npm run lint` | ESLint | | `npm run test` | Unit and component tests (Vitest) | | `npm run test:e2e` | End-to-end tests in a real browser (Playwright) | | `npm run format` | Prettier (write) | The end-to-end tests use a fake model API, so they need no key and cost nothing. They use an installed Chromium when there is one (or `E2E_CHROMIUM=/path/to/chrome`); otherwise run `npx playwright install chromium` once. ## Project notes - `graphify-out/` holds a knowledge graph of the codebase for quick navigation. See `AGENTS.md` for how it is used and refreshed. ## License [MIT](LICENSE) © 2026 Jee
